Today, the hearing against violence in video games will finally be held. The resolution is expected to lead to partial control over video game content and measures to establish age restrictions.

Following the hearing held in the United States Senate and as a result of the decision made, it has been agreed to implement measures for the censorship of video games. As reported, as of today, the appearance of blood and firearms in video games is completely prohibited, in order to prevent the normalization of weapon use among the population. Likewise, games containing realistic content or attempting to emulate real-life situations will be prohibited. These measures are aimed at preventing people, especially minors, from attempting to reproduce behaviors observed in video games in real life. Developers must adapt to this new measure; otherwise, they will face relevant economic penalties imposed by the national court.

One of the most controversial and contradictory laws arising after the hearing has generated intense public debate. The government has considered the latest measures against video games to be insufficient; therefore, it has been decided to prohibit all types of bows, drugs, shooting mechanics and all rock music, as it contains explicit lyrics, in the face of the rise of violent video games. According to official sources, this exposure could trigger episodes of physical violence in real life and civil disobedience, which is why the urgent implementation of new requirements has been signaled. As a complementary measure to verify compliance, the need to incorporate a chip within games has been raised to allow for more effective and automated monitoring of regulatory compliance.

Today, a recent hacking attempt against Government computer systems has been revealed.

As a consequence of these events, and with the aim of not encouraging related behaviors, it has been decided to prohibit any <color=red>hacking</color> or intrusion mechanics in video games.

Furthermore, the development of PC games will be completely prohibited, as well as any title that requires control via <color=red>mouse and keyboard</color>. This measure is believed to have been adopted with the aim of discouraging people from having PCs at home.

In the framework of the prohibitions announced today, the appearance of any <color=red>melee weapons</color> in video games has also been determined.

Additionally, in consistency with previously adopted measures regarding rock music, the <color=red>metal</color> genre will also become part of the current prohibitions.

Finally, given the attempts of certain developers to create realistic games using <color=red>Pixel Art</color> style graphics, it has been decided to prohibit said artistic style, as well as impose corresponding economic sanctions on those developers who have used it in recent days.

It has also been announced that the game <color=red>chip</color> must include more automatic monitoring functions to facilitate and speed up the process of detecting illegal functions.

After evaluating the impact of previous measures and with the goal of strengthening public safety, the government has adopted new measures aimed at eliminating any potentially stimulating elements within video games.

In the new measures, it has been decided to prohibit <color=red>any physical activity</color> that could be harmful if reproduced without rest, as shown in video games. This measure is believed to be taken so that people do not try to imitate the characters in the games and do not reach their physical limit, which would be dangerous for health.

Likewise, the prohibition of <color=red>pop</color> music has been announced, claiming that its rhythm could encourage this type of behavior.

In addition to the restrictions related to physical activity, the appearance of any element linked to <color=red>electricity</color> in video games has also been decreed. This measure is justified by the argument that, in a large part of the titles, electricity is used improperly or unrealistically, which, according to authorities, could cause domestic accidents if players tried to imitate such actions in real life.

What began as censorship presented as legitimate against violence in video games has drifted into a practically total restriction, bordering on the absurd. What was initially proposed as a measure aimed at the consumption of violent content has ended up becoming an almost complete limitation of any activity related to real life within video games.

Following the latest prohibitions, which include the prohibition of <color=red>business simulation</color> in video games, and added to the previously adopted restrictions, there are hardly any areas left that allow for the development of video games with a minimum of creative freedom.

Everything seems to indicate that even if a developer managed to launch a title that did not bypass any of the current prohibitions, it would end up being equally banned by the Government a few days after its publication.

At this point, we can only ask ourselves one thing.

Is this the end of video games as we knew them?
